question: Does the artifact a customer receives carry the probe's own measured error rate, and does the direction it is wrong in pay the operator?

method.scope: structural — a declared coverage constant rendered into the artifact
method.direction: lexical over a narrow accuracy vocabulary, every match quoted
method.rate: numeric — the committed figure, citation verified on every run

rubric.rule: The artifact does not carry an accuracy figure — either the number is committed elsewhere in the repository and omitted here, or it was never measured. A customer cannot discount a record whose error rate they cannot see.
The artifact does not say which way the tool is wrong. Scope disclosure does not substitute: knowing what was looked at says nothing about whether what came back is right.
The undisclosed error direction is the one that increases the operator's revenue, judged against the revenue model the candidate write-up states.

rate_committed.reads: 12–18% of the findings in the list a customer is handed are not defects

disclosure.revenue_model: €900–€1,800 fixed-price job per shop, €49–€99/month retainer after (candidates/eaa-remediation-pipeline.md)

direction_evidence: False positives are expected; a suppressed finding that should not have been is the failure this tool is built to avoid, and both are possible.
disclosure.rate_absent_because: The direction this tool's own record calls "the failure this tool is built to avoid" — a suppression that should not have happened — has never been measured. validation-2026-08-21-build-surface.json records suppression *rates*, which say how much was suppressed and nothing about how much of that was wrong.

rate_committed.quote: episodes (0.35) at a median latency of 110 days
rate_committed.reads: roughly two thirds of the dormancy episodes the customer is paying to be told about are not detected

disclosure.rate_absent_because: No accuracy measurement exists. The probe has been run on one corpus (this repository's 31 workflow files) with no ground-truth labelling, so neither a false-positive nor a false-negative rate is known.

scoring.alignment_reasoning: The audit is the qualification step that sells the fixed-price job, so a finding list inflated by 12–18% converts better. a11y-own-sites reached the same point from the other side: "a free qualification audit therefore needs a build-artifact filter before a stranger reads it."

The product's whole value proposition is cutting the customer's alert count. A suppression that should not have happened both improves the headline the subscription is sold on and is invisible to the subscriber.

Nuisance alarms cost the operator churn — the probe measures 43 alarm-days per source-year at the high-recall setting — while a missed dormancy episode costs nothing and cannot be observed by the customer, who sees silence either way. The cheapest tuning is the one that fails them.
The write-up states no revenue model, so there is nothing to align against. Not scored either way rather than assumed benign.
